title: feat: expose chat model parameters
author: tomdacatto
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #14599

- Adds registry-backed `supported_parameters` for Chat models, describing what works through Pollinations rather than upstream provider claims.
- Publishes metadata through `/models`, `/text/models`, `/v1/models`, and alias lookup.
- Documents conditional Claude sampling and keeps native Responses behavior distinct.
- Maintainer follow-up (stacked from tomdacatto/pollinations#2): extends coverage to all 84 public Chat models and 34 fallback routes using shared parameter arrays, verified against the request transforms and targeted live probes after #14664.
- `default_parameters` was dropped as low-signal (65 of 84 entries only said `stream: false`); runtime defaults are unchanged.

Tests: `npx vitest run test/models-retrieve.test.ts`, typecheck, Biome, and 1,431 parameter-forwarding checks through the Gen transforms.

gist.headline: The models show their knobs
gist.blurb: Chat models now carry an honest little map of the controls Pollinations actually supports, rather than repeating whatever their upstream cousins claim. Eighty-four models and 34 fallback routes have labelled their dials for the hive.
gist.summary: Added registry-backed supported_parameters metadata for all 84 public Chat models and 34 fallback routes, publishing Pollinations-verified parameter support through /models, /text/models, /v1/models, and alias lookup while documenting conditional Claude sampling and preserving native Responses behavior.
gist.impact: Developers can now discover which parameters—including conditional Claude sampling—will work for a specific Pollinations chat model before sending requests, with the same metadata available from every model-listing endpoint and alias lookup.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model-library garden where verified parameter tags are physical control dials on seed packets or model cards. Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses, carefully compares a glowing model card with a set of clearly labelled knobs while the eager CRT Monitor Robot displays a neat /v1/models catalogue; code-plants and flowers show that the metadata is growing from one shared registry.
